packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-24 -- first reader response (unverified image reading, UTF-8)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this text.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview of face 1)
- Parchment sheet, landscape, reused as an archival wrapper/cover: edges folded in (top, bottom, left and right turn-ins visible), vertical fold near centre; tie/sewing holes along the fold and at the right edge; small paper patches at left and right.
- Underlying text: a bifolium-like sheet with two text blocks, left and right of the central fold, written in a small, very faded brown/grey Gothic book hand, long lines (one column per half visible; possibly two columns per half -- not resolvable at overview scale). Ca. 40+ lines per block. No rubrics or enlarged initials visible at overview scale.
- Later additions in darker ink: large Fraktur-style title across top of right block, "Oberkellers Ambts" (reading tentative), with a flourish; a large looped symbol mid right block (looks like "S" or "fi" in a circle); a line of later cursive in the top turn-in at left ("...buch des ..."?); a modern pencil note at lower right turn-in ("Hans St... ...").
- Text also runs onto the left turn-in (left edge strip), i.e. the sheet was folded after writing.
- Interpretation (tentative): leaf of a medieval manuscript reused as a later administrative register cover.

TILE READINGS

--- image-002 (face 1, top-left tile: top turn-in, left turn-in, top-left of left text block) ---
Observation: ink is extremely faded grey on stained parchment; letter strokes are blurred. In the top turn-in (image-002 lines above the tear, approx. y 100-260) there is a line of later darker cursive, partly visible: "...[illegible] ...ff..." -- not readable at this tile.
Main block: ca. 13 ruled-looking text lines visible below the tear (y 380-1340), with a left text edge at about x 480 and text continuing on the left turn-in (x 180-340).
Crops made: rscratch/packet-24/002-blue.jpg (blue channel, useless: noise), rscratch/packet-24/002-red.jpg (red channel, blur 1, autocontrast -- best), rscratch/packet-24/002-red-mirror.jpg (mirrored test).
On the red-channel crop the letter shapes do not resolve into a consistent script read left-to-right; the mirrored crop looks somewhat more like a cursive Gothic hand. Tentative observation: much of what is visible on this face may be show-through/offset of writing from the other face, or the writing is abraded to the point of illegibility. I could not read any word with confidence on this tile.
image-002 lines 1-13 (main block): [illegible]

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-014, overview of face 2) -- written before returning to face-1 tiles
- Same sheet, other side (pencil shelfmark-like note at lower right turn-in, "...Fragm. 193v"? -- tentative). Landscape; turn-ins and central vertical fold as on face 1.
- Text: a single document written in a vernacular (German-looking) 16th-century-style cursive (Kurrent-type) hand in brown/grey ink, long lines running across BOTH halves of the sheet on each line? -- Uncertain: there are two blocks, left and right of the fold; the left block's lines look like they end at the fold and the right block is separate. On closer inspection the lines at the bottom ("...Nuremberg... Christi ... Clöster" on the right) and the left block's last line ("...hab(e)n ...") are at the same height, which is consistent with either one wide block across the fold or two pages. To be checked on tiles.
- Ca. 30-35 lines per block; text ends about 3/4 down, with a large flourish/paraph and a short stroke below at right. No rubrics.
- Left margin: a later pen sketch of looped figure (two loops, "8"-like) at x ~360-410.
- Face 2 ink is markedly darker than face 1. Tentative interpretation: face 1's faint "text" is largely show-through of face 2 plus an abraded original text; the mirrored crop of image-002 looked more script-like, supporting show-through.

--- image-017 (face 2, top row, third tile from left: just right of central fold, top of right half) ---
Observations: the central fold runs vertically at x ~180-200; text on the left of the fold (x 0-180) is the end of lines coming from the left half, and lines appear to continue across the fold at the same baselines -> tentatively ONE document whose lines run the full width of the sheet (not two pages). Hand: German cursive (Kurrent), brown ink, with some strokes faded to blue-grey; long looped ascenders on d, h, l; "vnnd" with doubled n; virgula "/" as punctuation (rendered "/" below). A large looped flourish rises from line 1 into the top margin (x ~800-1200).
Crop: rscratch/packet-24/017-top-blue.jpg (blue channel; suppresses the grey strokes -- less useful than the original).
